name: efficient_vs_charging_terminal
drive_hint: Tap each line once with the same amplitude and compare: the top line's brightness/energy dumps out almost immediately (half-life ~57 steps); the bottom line visibly keeps glowing/ringing far longer (half-life ~206 steps) before it discharges.
notes: Two side-by-side lines, same shape, only rad_admittance_fraction differs. Good side-by-side teaching scenario for the emitter/storage tradeoff (§2.4).

name: shield_impedance_step
drive_hint: Tap the left (low-impedance) end. Most of the injected energy stays on the near side and keeps ringing there instead of reaching the far end -- an incoming attack drawn to hit the near side is mostly reflected before it reaches whatever the far segment is protecting.
notes: Z ratio 9 (20 vs 180) measured far/near radiated-energy ratio 2.29, clearly weaker transmission than the ratio=1 control (1.29). Direction confirmed, exact reflection fraction is confounded by both terminals' own Y_rad -- see kinetic_thermal_shield.md §2 caveat.

name: charge_and_release_loop
drive_hint: Repeatedly tap SPACE ~15-25 times at a steady rhythm (period ~93 steps / ~0.93s at this radius's f0) -- sigil_lab.py's _inject_burst now targets the loop-closing junction automatically, not the tail terminal. Energy visibly builds in the loop over the taps, then stop tapping and watch it drain out through the tail tip as a sustained (not instant) glow.
notes: Peak charged energy 0.220 over 25 on-beat taps; only ~1.1% of that comes back out as radiation before the rest dissipates as ink damping -- reads as 'the loop gets warm/charged, then slowly bleeds out a modest glow' rather than a sharp release burst. For a punchier release, pair with a much lower rad_admittance_fraction (already at 0.05) or accept this is closer to 'slow discharge' than 'burst' with default damping -- see md for the damping-vs-charge-time tradeoff.

name: fire_vs_force_ink_range
drive_hint: Tap the left end of each 500px line and compare far-end brightness: force-ink arrives at the far end almost undiminished (98.8% of tap amplitude); fire-ink arrives nearly dead (2% of tap amplitude) -- a visceral side-by-side of 'kinetic sigils can sprawl, heat sigils must stay compact' (§2.5).
notes: Same two ink presets recommended as defaults for a force/fire element pair. Crossover where the difference becomes obvious to a player is ~200-300px.
